 J U D G M E N T

This petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed by the Petitioners seeking compensation of .30,00,000/ for the death of Shri Marisiddegowda S/o Late Siddegowda in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 11.10.2021, at about 7.30 p.m., Martisiddegowda @
Gavisiddegowda was pedestrian on extreme side of Kanakapura - Kodihalli road, by observing all vehicular movements and cautiously.

When he reached near Ankacharidoddi gate, Kasaba Hobali,
Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time, the rider of Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA05LF0989 (herein after called as alleged offending vehicle), ridden the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, thereby dashed against said Marisiddegowda.
Due to the accident, Marisiddegowda sustained severe injuries all over the body and succumbed to the fatal injuries at the spot.
Immediately, he was taken to Government hospital, Kanakapura, wherein postmortem was conducted.
Thereafter, the petitioner have performed funeral and obsequies ceremony by incurring Rs.2,00,000/ including transportation charges etc.

Smt. Suma vs Sarvesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186218699/
2 3.
At the time of accident, Marisiddegowda was aged about 54 years, he was an agriculturist and earning a sum of .25,000/ per month.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased and they were depending upon the income of deceased and due to untimely death of Marisiddegowda, they have suffered mental shock and agony and lost their bread earner of the family.
4.
Further, the petitioners stated that the accident and death was due to negligence of the driver of the alleged offending vehicle.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the alleged offending vehicle are liable to pay compensation.
5. In response to the petition notice, both the Respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statements.
6. Respondent No.1who is RC owner of the offending vehicle has denied the petition averments.
He has admitted that offending vehicle belongs to him and it was insured with the Respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident and it is a 5 years policy.
Further submitted that, the driver who drove the offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

He has denied the negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle and deceased himself has not followed the vehicle movements while walking on the said road along with intoxication of alcohol and unbalancing of his body, at that time an unnumbered Pulser motor cycle came and hit to the detaching from the road side tree and because of that reason, they have implicated the motor cycle in the alleged accident, colluding with the police and because of that reasons, they have lodged the complaint after lapse of one day of the alleged accident.
Further, he has denied the age, occupation, income of deceased, relationship of Petitioners with the deceased and dependency upon the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the Petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant and prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. Respondent No.2insurance company in its objection statement denied the contents of petition averments, strongly denied the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle.
However its liability is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has contended that the owner of the alleged vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions as required under Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

It is the main contention of the respondent that, the alleged accident has occurred solely due to negligence of deceased himself, being the pedestrian was crossing the road without having proper look out vehicular movements of the road and in a place where not meant for pedestrian crossing and caused the accident.

It has contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid DL at the time of accident and respondent No.1 by entrusting and allowing rider to ride offending vehicle, without holding valid and effective DL, has thereby contravened the terms and conditions of the policy and as such the respondent is liable to indemnify.
It has also denied all the allegations with regard to the age, avocation and income of the deceased, relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased and their dependency.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

Smt. Suma vs Sarvesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186218699/
3 8.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following Issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioners proves that the death of Sri.Marsiddegowda S/o. Late Siddegowda was only due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of Motor cycle bearing No.KA05 LF0989 on 11.10.2021 at about 7.30 p.m., near Ankacharidoddi Gate, Kasaba Hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District ?
2. What compensation Petitioners are entitled?
3. What order?
9. In support of their claim, 1st Petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.15.
In addition to her evidence, examined an eyewitness by name Chaluvaraju as PW2.

At the time of his evidence, he got marked one document as Ex.P.16.
10.
On the other hand, the Respondent insurance company has not adduced any oral or documentary evidence.
11. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

12. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly In the Affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 13. ISSUE NO.1: Petitioners say that on 11.10.2021, at 7.30 p.m., Marisiddegowda @
Gavisiddegowda was pedestrian on extreme left side of Kanakapura - Kodihalli road, by observing all vehicular movements and cautiously.

When he reached near Ankacharidoddi gate, Kasaba Hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, the rider of offending Motor cycle, rode the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against said Marisiddegowda.
Due to the accident, Marisiddegowda sustained severe injuries all over the body and succumbed to the fatal injuries at the spot.
Petitioners say that it was the negligence of the rider of the offending Motor cycle.
They relied on the police records and submitted that the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
14. To prove the negligence on the part rider of the alleged offending vehicle, Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW1.
She is not an eyewitness and she relied on the police records.

In support of their version Petitioners have produced FIR, Complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report,
Inquest report, PM report, notice U/s.133 of MV Act, Reply notice, Bail bond surety of accused, and Smt. Suma vs Sarvesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186218699/
4 charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 11.
She relied on the police records to show the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
15. In support of their version, the Petitioners have examined one eyewitness to the accident by name Chaluvaraj as PW2.

He has stated that on the alleged date, time and place of accident, he was going towards his hotel from the sericulture house, at the same time he noticed that deceased was pedestrian on extreme left side of the road, at that time the rider of Yamaha Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA05LF--0989 came at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased from behind who was walking on the correct side of the road.
PW2 has stated that the accident has occurred due to sole rash and negligent riding of the rider of the said motor cycle.
Though the counsel for Respondent No.2 has crossexamined the PW2, but nothing has been elicited to disbelieve his version.
16. It is contended by Respondent No.2 that due to negligence of deceased the accident occurred.
It is contended that deceased was crossing the road without observing the vehicles.
In the cross examination of PW2, it was suggested that deceased himself was the rider of the alleged offending motor cycle and due to his negligence he fell down and sustained injuries and died.
It is alleged that,
later, by colluding with police false complaint is given stating that he was walking on the road.
PW1 and PW2 have denied it and stated that it was the negligence of Motor cycle rider.
Absolutely there are no evidences to show the negligence of deceased.
The Respondent No.2 has not examined the rider of the offending motor cycle and not produced any materials to prove its contention.
It is also contended that since the deceased was walking on the highway and was trying to cross the highway where there is no provision, it is sought to consider contributory negligence.
Absolutely there are no evidences to show that he was crossing the road and the accident has occurred at the extreme left side of the road.
Hence, the contributory negligence cannot be considered.
Except filing of written statement, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral or documentary evidence to rebut the case of the petitioners and to prove the defences.
17. All the evidence and materials clearly indicate that it was negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle.
After investigation police have filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle.
Absolutely there are no materials to overcome the findings in the charge sheet.
On perusal of medical and police records there are no materials to show the negligence of the deceased.
No negligence of the deceased can be attributed.
Considering all the above materials, I hold it was the negligence of only on the part of rider of the offending motor cycle and I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2:
The Petitioners state that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Marisiddegowda.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 is son and the petitioner No.3 is the daughter of the deceased.
They have produced the Aadhaar cards at Ex.P.12 to 15 which clearly indicate that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased Marisiddegowda.
Therefore, the Petitioners being wife and children of deceased are all considered as legal heirs of the deceased.
The children are major and are above 25 years.
3rd petitioner is married and 2nd petitioner is also working.
By the evidence, it could be seen that the second petitioner was residing with the deceased.

As the income of the 2nd petitioner is not proved and in Smt. Suma vs Sarvesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186218699/
5 the complaint itself, he has stated that he was also doing coolie with his parents, he is considered a dependant.

entities.text: Smt. Suma vs Sarvesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The 3rd petitioner being married and residing separately is not considered as dependent of deceased and she is entitled only for compensation under loss of consortium and loss to estate.

19. It is stated that at the time of accident, the deceased Marisiddegowda was aged 54 years, he was an agriculturist and earning a sum of .25,000/p.m. and he was the sole earning member of the family.
There is no supportive documents to show the avocation and income of the deceased.
Hence there is no proof of avocation and income of the deceased.

In the absence of proof of income,
notional income of .15,000/ per month is taken.

20. According to the Ex.P.15Aadhaar card of the deceased, his date of birth is mentioned as 6.4.1967 and as such he was aged 54 years and the same is considered as age of the deceased as on the date of accident and proper multiplier applicable to the case is 11.
As the age of the deceased is between 5060 years, 10% future prospects is to be added as per Pranay Sethi's case.

Hence, if 10%
added to the income of the deceased, it works out to Rs.16,500/ (15,000/ + 1,500/).

As wife and son are considered as dependents, 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, then it works out to Rs.11,000/(16,500/ (-) 5,500/) and the annual income would come to .11,000x12=1,32,000/ and applying 11 multiplier, the loss of dependency would be .14,52,000/.
21. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others.1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled .40,000/ each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 22. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father.

Hence,
.20,000/ towards loss to estate.
23. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses:

Petitioners have claimed that they have spent .2,00,000/ towards transportation of dead 1 (2018) 18 SCC 130 body, funeral &
obsequies and other incidental expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances, it would be proper to award .15,000/ for the transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.
24. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
Sl . Compensation heads Amount No.

1. Loss of dependency . 14,52,000/
2. Loss of Consortium . 1,20,000/
3. Loss to estate .

Smt. Suma vs Sarvesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186218699/
6 4. Transportation of . 15,000/ dead body and Funeral Expenses Total .
Liability:
The petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent riding of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of being the insured and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, in view of the valid issuance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the compensation and pay the petitioners with interest.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within three months from the date of this Order.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
26. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
 Petitioners

are awarded  compensation of Rs.16,07,000/
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall  deposit the compensation amount within three months from the date of this Order.
After deposit of amount, 50% of the amount is apportioned to petitioner No.1 and 25% each to the Petitioner No.2 and 3.

Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of petitioner No.1, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to her through E payment on proper identification.
Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.2 and 3, entire amount with interest shall be disbursed to them through Epayment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at  .1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father.

Hence,
.20,000/ towards loss to estate.
23. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses:

Petitioners have claimed that they have spent .2,00,000/ towards transportation of dead 1 (2018) 18 SCC 130 body, funeral &
obsequies and other incidental expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances, it would be proper to award .15,000/ for the transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.
24. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :

1. Loss of dependency . 14,52,000/
2. Loss of Consortium . 1,20,000/
3. Loss to estate .
Liability:
The policy was in force as on the date of being the insured and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, in view of the valid issuance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the compensation and pay the petitioners with interest.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within three months from the date of this Order.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
26. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
 Petitioners

are awarded  compensation of Rs.16,07,000/
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall  deposit the compensation amount within three months from the date of this Order.
After deposit of amount, 50% of the amount is apportioned to petitioner No.1 and 25% each to the Petitioner No.2 and 3.

Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of petitioner No.1, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to her through E payment on proper identification.
Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.2 and 3, entire amount with interest shall be disbursed to them through Epayment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at  .1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
